issues.description: Resolver silently drops the post-condition that requirements are fully prepared, pushing an implicit protocol onto every caller.
issues.detail: The deleted block in resolver.py used to set req.prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False. Now install/download/wheel each must call prepare_linked_requirements_more, and any other consumer of RequirementSet (extensions, future commands, tests) inherits half-prepared state. Either restore enforcement in the resolver, document the contract loudly, or assert it at the boundary.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist caches a metadata-only distribution with no invalidation or documented precedence after full preparation.
issues.detail: get_dist now returns self._distribution before checking metadata_directory or local_file_path, but nothing invalidates the cached metadata-only dist once the real wheel lands. If the two diverge (RECORD, file list) callers silently see stale data. Pick one canonical dist field, or invalidate/upgrade the cache on full prepare and document precedence.

issues.description: Identical prepare_linked_requirements_more call copy-pasted into three commands instead of one shared helper.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each now open their post-resolve block with the same line. The next command (pip lock, the very motivator) will forget it. Extract a finish_preparation helper, or push the call back behind a dry_run flag in resolve(). Copy-paste across call sites is not decoupling.

issues.description: download_info backfill inside _fetch_metadata_only entangles two concerns and is unsafe when source_dir is missing.
issues.detail: prepare_linked_requirement now both fetches metadata and synthesizes download_info via direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir). In dry-run source_dir may be unset, and the if-None guard hides ordering bugs. The contract for download_info in the metadata-only path is undocumented. Separate the two outputs or set download_info at the single site that needs it.

issues.description: No visible test proves --dry-run actually avoids downloading the wheel.
issues.detail: The headline behavior is one assertion: run --dry-run against a PEP-658 wheel and confirm the wheel bytes were never fetched. The diff ships zero such test, so a future refactor silently reintroduces the regression. Add a test that fails on the old behavior and passes on the new one, ideally also covering VCS URLs and --report.

issues.description: Patch bundles two distinct changes: the dry-run resolver fix and download_info plumbing for pip lock/--report.
issues.detail: The news entry itself names both behaviors. Splitting into two patches makes review and revert tractable: one moves the eager prepare out of the resolver, the other adds download_info population for metadata-only fetches. As one patch it is harder to bisect when either half regresses.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the direction is right: removing the eager full-download from the resolver is overdue, and dry-run/lock benefit from PEP-658 metadata-only fetches. But execution leaks an implicit protocol onto callers by silently dropping the resolver's post-condition, copy-pastes the replacement call across three commands, and adds a cached metadata-only distribution with no invalidation or precedence story. The download_info backfill mixes concerns and is unsafe under dry-run with missing source_dir. Most damning: no test pins the headline behavior. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — restore or document the invariant, consolidate the call site, fix the cache contract, split the patch, and add a regression test.
